newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sets base prices for B Band concessions.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sets base prices for B Band concessions.

text.p: Brazil set a 600 million-real base price for a concession to operate cellular services on the B Band frequency in metropolitan Sao Paulo and established base prices for nine other concession areas across the country.

Bid specifications made avaliable Monday by the Communications Ministry also stipulated that 40 percent of the concession purchase prices would be due upon signing of concession contracts. The tender details are avaliable at the ministry for 200 reais or on the Internet at http:/w.w.w.mc.gov.br, according to officials.

The government said last week it plans to take bids March 31 on 15-year contracts to operate B Band cellular services in 10 regions nationwide in the first opening of Brazil's promising cellular market to foreign capital.
Some 20 consortia, comprised of foreign and local firms, expect to compete in the bidding and winners will be picked based on which offers the highest concession price as well as the lowest tariffs.
According to the bid specifications, 60 percent of the purchase price must be paid in three equal annual installments.
The payments will be adjusted for inflation according to the IGP-DI inflation index of the Getulio Vargas Foundation and carry a one-percent monthly interest rate, it said.

The government also set a 600 million-real base price on the B Band concession for the rest of Sao Paulo state and 500 million reais for the concession area encompassing Rio de Janeiro and Espiritu Santo states.
It set the following base prices for the remaining seven concessions:
Minas Gerais state: 400 million reais.
Parana and Santa Catarina states: 330 million reais.
Rio Grande do Sul state: 330 million reais.
Goais, Tocantins, Mato Grosso, Rondonia and Acre states and the federal district: 270 million reais.
Amazonas, Roraima, Amapa, Para and Maranhao states: 200 million reais.
Bahia and Sergipe states: 230 million reais.
Piaui, Ceara, Rio Grande do Norte, Paraiba, Pernambuco and Alagoas states: 230 million reais.
The bid documents also outlined the minimum number of cellular terminals that concession holders must install in each of the 10 regions.
For instance, in the metropolitan Sao Paulo area, the contract winner must install a minimum 1.8 million terminals.

Meanwhile, the government stipulates that Brazilians must own at least 51 percent of the capital stock of a consortium operating B Band cellular services, limiting foreign investors to no more than 49 percent.
The tender rules, included in four phone book-sized catalogues, are avaliable at the ministry for 200 reais or on the Internet at http:/w.w.w.mc.gov.br, according to officials.
((--Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 248 5413))
